subject: Cross-region demo scheduling: Avatech & Redwood — timezone coordination
messages:
From: Samantha Hayes <samantha.hayes@avatech.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Feb 2027 09:03:00 -0800
Subject: Intro + demo request (Avatech)

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the quick intro to Redwood — we've been evaluating inference platforms and would like a product demo next week focused on latency/cost for small-batch real-time inference. We're based in SF (PST). Ideally we'd do a session with engineering + procurement (Tom Liu, cc'd) — 45 minutes + 15 for Q&A.

We realize your team has EU coverage and timezone overlaps can be tricky. Would an early-morning Redwood engineer work (your time) for a late afternoon in PST? Our initial target slots: Tue/Wed/Thu next week at 10:00 AM or 11:30 AM PST.

Can you confirm availability and whether you can include someone from solutions engineering who can go into perf/quantization tradeoffs? Also any timezone caveats re: daylight savings around March would be good to call out.

Thanks,
Sam

Samantha Hayes
Head of Infrastructure, Avatech
Samantha.Hayes@avatech.com
+1 (415) 555-0198

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Hayes <samantha.hayes@avatech.com>
Cc: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Feb 2027 19:12:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Intro + demo request (Avatech)

Hi Sam — great to hear from you, we'd love to run this. Thanks for flagging the timezone/DST thing — US DST starts in March and CET shifts later in March, so for sessions in Feb the offsets are stable (PST = UTC-8, CET = UTC+1).

We can cover latency, cost, and quantization tradeoffs — I'll bring Lukas (Solutions Eng) to go deep on kernels/quant profiles. Jonas (head of trust) is on cc in case you want any quick security/compliance context.

Two suggested slots that map to your PST times:
- Tue Feb 16, 10:00 AM PST / Tue Feb 16, 19:00 CET (45 min)
- Tue Feb 16, 11:30 AM PST / Tue Feb 16, 20:30 CET (45 min)

If either works, I'll send a calendar invite and attach the short demo deck. I'll also include an .ics with both time options to make it easy to add. If you prefer a different day, happy to adjust.

Best,
Marissa

--
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +44 20 7946 0123

From: Samantha Hayes <samantha.hayes@avatech.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Liu <tom.liu@avatech.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Feb 2027 10:50:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Intro + demo request (Avatech)

Marissa — thanks, both slots look good. Prefer the 11:30 AM PST / 20:30 CET option so our engineering lead (in SF) can join after a planning workshop. Could you please: 
- Send calendar invite for Tue Feb 16 at 11:30 AM PST (20:30 CET)
- Add an agenda and the short deck so we can share with our team

Tom (cc) will handle procurement logistics; if you have any docs we should review beforehand (SLA/retention), please include.

Appreciate the DST note — we may run additional sessions in March so will check again then.

Best,
Sam

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Hayes <samantha.hayes@avatech.com>
Cc: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Feb 2027 20:10:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Intro + demo request (Avatech)

Perfect — sending invite now. Attaching: redwood-demo-deck.pdf (preview) and demo-availability.ics (both options). Agenda (short):
1) 10 min - intro & goals (Marissa)
2) 25 min - runtime/quant & perf deep-dive (Lukas)
3) 10 min - security/compliance & next steps (Jonas)

Procurement notes: I'll include a link to our standard SLA and SOC 2 summary in the calendar description. For procurement, Tom, if you'd like a one-pager ahead of time I can loop in our sales ops.

Invite link: https://meet.redwood.com/avt-demo-AV-4021
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/AV-4021

--
Marissa

Thanks Marissa — I'll be on the call for the perf/quant section. Note for everyone's calendars: 11:30 AM PST = 20:30 CET (we're in CET at the moment). I added both slots to my calendar in case we need to swap. Will prepare two short benchmark slides comparing int8 vs 4-bit quant for the model family you mentioned.
